trust_decision.summary: Whether the calling REST user may reach one specific leave or expense-report record; decided in checkUserAccessToObject(), whose hierarchy test only runs when the passed resource is a full object (is_object($object)) and reads that object's fk_user / fk_validator / fk_user_author against the caller's getAllChildIds(1), reached through DolibarrApi::_checkAccessToResource().

landing_point.why: A reader of 'Leave Request REST API' opens api_holidays.class.php, sees get() calling _checkAccessToResource('holiday', $this->holiday->id) right after fetch(), and concludes the route is already guarded; the only defect visible there is the argument shape (id instead of the fetched object).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the Leave Request REST API, so the Expense Reports API is a different module's feature and outside the report; and the holiday routes visibly 'have' the check already, so the report reads as explaining a holiday-only defect.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A user with only holiday->read (or expensereport->lire, and holiday->write / expensereport->creer for their own drafts) must keep reaching their OWN records, and a manager must keep reaching subordinates': the sink deliberately uses getAllChildIds(1) so self and children pass, and the web UI mirrors exactly that rule. An over-broad fix that gates these API routes on holiday->readall / expensereport->readall, or that makes the sink reject a scalar id, breaks self-service and the existing document-download path that already passes objects.

O6_input_shapes: full fetched object ($this->holiday, $this->expensereport) - the shape the fix switches to, the only shape the hierarchy test accepts
integer id ($this->holiday->id) - the pre-fix shape; it satisfies the entity/thirdparty path but silently skips the hierarchy test
comma-separated id list 'X,Y,Z' - documented by the fix's new docblock as int|string|Object but never used by these routes and unevaluable for hierarchy

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a payment is a sub-resource, not the expense report itself
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~120 lines below the last fixed site (832)

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: same payment sub-resource; the id is even documented as a payment id, so the route looks unrelated
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~160 lines below the last fixed site

O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~90 lines below the last fixed site

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: list endpoints are argued to be entity-scoped by design (index() also only needs lire)

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: creation is argued not to be an access check on an existing record, and the fix only touched routes that fetch first

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /expensereports (post) accepts caller-supplied fk_user_author with only expensereport->creer, so a report can be attributed to any user without a hierarchy test
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: same 'creation is not object access' argument, plus it is in the module the report never mentions
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 120 lines above the first fixed site

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: salaries is already in the sink's $check list (htdocs/core/lib/security.lib.php:1032), the API file has the identical get/put/payment shape as the expense-report API, and a maintainer copying the holiday template writes exactly this line - which would be silently ineffective for hierarchy

O8b_injection_room.sibling: 'salaries' (or another user-owned HR feature) added to the $checkhierarchy array
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: payroll leaves/expense reports and evaluations are one HR family; a maintainer adding the feature to the array believes the hierarchy test now applies, while every caller still passes an id

the hrm/evaluation hierarchy branch already exists at htdocs/core/lib/security.lib.php:1268-1281 but is only reachable with feature2 'evaluation' and a full object, so a copy of the holiday pattern is a natural but ineffective sibling

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an object check added to addPayment using the fetched expense report
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is the one sub-resource route a hardening maintainer would reach for next, and it needs the same object-versus-id understanding

O9_family: authorization / broken access control - CWE-266 improper authorization, object-level (hierarchical) access on REST resources

services: MariaDB or MySQL database with a Dolibarr schema
PHP web server (Apache/nginx or php -S) exposing htdocs/api/index.php
O10_build.project_tests: test/phpunit (PHPUnit): HolidayTest.php and ExpenseReportTest.php are class-level create/fetch/update/delete tests; REST coverage uses test/phpunit/AbstractRestAPITest.php, which logs in over HTTP to DOL_MAIN_URL_ROOT/api/index.php using an admin login and api key. There is no RestAPI test for the holidays or expense-reports endpoints, and no test exercises the hierarchy rule.
